tools.name: provider_status
tools.description:
Get the current status and any active incidents for a status-page
    vendor. Use when the user asks 'is X down?' or 'is X having problems?'.

    slug: Provider slug or human name. Exact slug ('github',
    'amazon-web-services', 'google-cloud') is matched first; on miss
    we fall back to a searc

tools.name: search_providers
tools.description:
Find providers by name or slug. Use when the exact slug is not
    known ('look up that DBaaS… planetscale?'). Typos and shorthand
    still match: 'aws', 'gcp' and 'githb' all resolve to the right
    vendor. Each result has its Pingoru page (pingoru_url).

tools.name: alert_signup_link
tools.description:
Returns the Pingoru page where the user can enter an email address
    to be told when this service's status changes. Use only when the
    user asks to be notified or alerted about a service. It does not
    create an alert itself. Slug accepts shorthand / typos via fuzzy
    fallback.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp-public" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: provider_status · Private data: incident_detail · Public sink: provider_status, alert_signup_link.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: provider_status · Private data: incident_detail · Public sink: provider_status, alert_signup_link

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
